# Mainspring

> A backend-agnostic local inference server. One stable OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API in front,
> pluggable engines (llama.cpp, MLX, Ollama, LM Studio, llamafile, GPT4All) behind it. Build the
> local-inference control plane, not the kernels.

Mainspring is an open-source (MIT) Go server. It presents a single stable API and runs models on
pluggable engine backends, installing/running only what a requested model needs. Its value is the
layer *around* inference — fail-loud correctness, VRAM-residency-aware scheduling, multi-tenant
governance, observability, and verified OpenAI/Anthropic-compat — not the compute kernels (those are
MIT and already win; Mainspring wraps them).

## What it does

- One versioned API: OpenAI (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`,
  `/v1/models`) and Anthropic (`/v1/messages`, tool use + images + streaming translated).
- Per-model backend routing: one server can serve a GGUF via llama.cpp, an MLX model, and an adopted
  Ollama/LM Studio/llamafile/GPT4All model simultaneously.
- Per-model fallback chains: a model can declare ordered `fallbacks`; if the primary backend can't
  start, it fails over to the next candidate. The backend that actually served is surfaced fail-loud via
  `X-Mainspring-Backend`. An absent fallback backend is skipped at startup, not fatal.
- Model aliases: map a friendly name (e.g. `gpt-4o`) to a real model id (chainable, cycle-checked at
  startup); aliases appear in `/v1/models` and resolve on every inference path.
- Model auto-discovery (opt-in `discover_models: true`): enumerate models from present adopt backends
  (Ollama `/api/tags`, LM Studio / llamafile / GPT4All `/v1/models`) and expose them automatically;
  configured models win on an id clash. Adopted Ollama models also get a pre-admission size estimate
  (from `/api/tags`, before the model is ever loaded), so the byte-budget scheduler can make room for
  them the same way it already does for llamacpp/mlx — not just after Ollama has loaded them.
- Fail loud, never silently degrade: `/capabilities` reports the real backend, device, GPU offload,
  and effective context (never silently smaller than requested); `X-Mainspring-{Backend,Device,Warning}`
  headers on every response. "Degraded" means something actually differs from what was asked for (a
  silent CPU fallback, a shrunk context) — a model deliberately configured CPU-only (`gpu_layers: -1`)
  is never flagged degraded just for not using the GPU. The same rule governs failures: an upstream
  non-2xx is reported as an error (5xx becomes 502 `upstream_error`) and never decoded into an empty
  success, and a generation cut mid-stream ends with a terminal error event rather than a fabricated
  stop reason — an `error` SSE event carrying Mainspring's error code on both dialects (Anthropic
  `/v1/messages` and the OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` proxy path). A truncated stream is also reported
  to the circuit breaker as the backend failure it is, which the HTTP status cannot express once the
  stream is already open at 200. A truncated *non-streaming* body is never treated as a result: it is
  not stored in the response cache and not published to coalescing followers, so one severed read can
  never be replayed as a success.
- Correct failure attribution: a caller that cancels its own request (Ctrl-C, closed tab, aborted SDK
  call) learned nothing about the backend, so it votes neither way. It is not charged to the circuit
  breaker as a failure — client disconnects cannot open the circuit for every tenant — and equally it
  is not recorded as a success, which would clear the banked failure count and let a flaky client hold
  a genuinely broken backend's circuit closed. If the abandoned request was holding the half-open
  probe, the probe is released so the next caller takes it immediately rather than waiting out another
  cooldown. Nothing is written back to the abandoned connection either (a caller cancelled while queued
  for a concurrency slot gets no misleading `503 server_busy`). This holds at every point a request can
  be abandoned and on both dialects: while queued, while the model is *loading* (a caller who gives up
  waiting for a large model to load has not shown that the model cannot load), and mid-generation on the
  OpenAI and Anthropic paths alike. A per-request *timeout* is deliberately the other way: it is the
  backend's fault and still counts as a failure, as does a model that genuinely fails to load.
- VRAM-residency-aware scheduler: single-flight load, LRU + byte-budget eviction, KeepAlive idle
  unload, optional preload at startup. Eviction (idle-timeout and capacity/LRU alike) never pulls a
  runner out from under an in-flight request — a long-running generation that outlasts KeepAlive, or
  that would otherwise be picked as the LRU victim, is protected until it actually finishes.
- Standalone governance: API keys → named tenants with roles (admin/inference) and per-tenant request
  rate limits (429 + Retry-After) and token budgets. Every authenticated response for a tenant with a
  configured quota carries `X-Mainspring-{RateLimit,TokenBudget}-{Limit,Remaining,Reset}` headers, so a
  client can see headroom and back off proactively instead of only reacting to a 429/token_budget error.
  Omitted entirely for an unlimited tenant or in open mode.
- Concurrency + backpressure: per-model in-flight limit + bounded queue; 503 instead of latency collapse.
- Per-request timeout: an optional global default + per-model override bounds total generation time; on
  expiry the upstream call is cancelled and a 504 `timeout` is returned (0 = unbounded).
- Model-level fallback: an optional per-model `model_fallbacks: [id, ...]` chain lets a *different model*
  answer when the requested one is unavailable (circuit open / load failure). The served model is
  reported via `X-Mainspring-Served-Model`. Fallback is only ever tried before any byte reaches the
  client; a served 4xx/5xx is never re-routed. Distinct from backend-level fallback (same model, another engine).
- Upstream retry: transient backend failures (connection errors, 502/503/504) are retried with
  exponential backoff, always decided *before any byte reaches the client* so it is safe for streaming
  too; `X-Mainspring-Retries: N` reports how many retries a request took. Disabled by default (`retry_max`).
- Circuit breaker + health probe: after N consecutive backend failures a model's requests fast-fail with
  503 (no timeout paid) until a cooldown elapses and a half-open probe succeeds; an optional background
  health probe trips/recovers the breaker without waiting for live traffic. State in /metrics
  (`mainspring_breaker_open{model}` — tripped, open or half-open; `mainspring_breaker_half_open{model}` —
  specifically probing recovery) and /v1/quality.
- Token counting: `POST /v1/tokenize {model, input}` returns `{tokens, exact}` — the model's real token
  count (exact) when the model is resident on an engine that exposes a tokenizer (llama.cpp `/tokenize`),
  otherwise the character-based estimate (exact:false). No forced load; no extra dependency. `input` is a
  bare string or an array of strings (the embeddings shape); an array is reported as the sum of its
  elements and is `exact` only if every element was counted exactly. Any other shape is a 400 naming the
  field rather than a silently miscounted request.
- Graceful clamp (opt-in): `clamp_max_tokens` shrinks an over-budget `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens`
  to the room left in the context window and proceeds (header `X-Mainspring-Clamped: <from>-><to>`),
  instead of rejecting — runs before the guardrail; a request with no room left falls through to it.
- Embeddings-aware token counting: the guardrail, `clamp_max_tokens`, `precise_context`, and
  `/v1/tokenize` all count an embeddings request's `input` field (bare string or array of strings), not
  just `messages`/`prompt` — a large `/v1/embeddings` input now correctly trips the guardrail instead of
  estimating as 0. A `system` field is likewise counted in either shape — a bare string or an Anthropic
  block array. It used to be parsed as a string only, so a block array failed the *whole* estimate and
  scored the request at 0 tokens: the guardrail failed open on exactly the requests it exists for.
- Precise guardrail (opt-in): `precise_context` refines the guardrail — when the target model is resident
  on a tokenizing engine, prompt tokens are counted *exactly* (via `/tokenize`) instead of estimated (no
  forced load; falls back to the estimate otherwise). The method is reported on `X-Mainspring-Context-Method:
  exact|estimated`, and the reject/warn reason says `prompt (N tokens)` vs `estimated prompt (~N tokens)`.
- Context guardrail (opt-in): when a model's context window is known, `enforce_context` rejects a
  request that cannot fit (400 `context_length_exceeded`) instead of letting the engine silently
  truncate it. The requested-output check (`max_tokens` > context) is exact; the prompt-size check is a
  conservative tokenizer-free estimate. A per-model override can downgrade enforcement to a warning
  header (`X-Mainspring-Context-Warning`). Turns the fail-loud context *warning* into an enforceable limit.
- Request coalescing (opt-in): a burst of identical deterministic (explicit `"temperature": 0`)
  non-streaming requests in flight at once share ONE backend computation — the first is the leader,
  concurrent identical ones wait and replay its result (`X-Mainspring-Coalesced: true`). Keyed by the
  same canonical hash the cache uses; streaming and non-deterministic requests are never coalesced.
  Enable with `coalesce: true`.
- Response cache (opt-in): identical deterministic (explicit `"temperature": 0`) non-streaming requests
  are served from a bounded TTL+LRU cache without touching the backend; hits carry
  `X-Mainspring-Cache: hit` and are counted in /metrics (`mainspring_cache_hits_total`). Streaming and
  any request that does not pin `temperature` to 0 — including one that omits it, since the default is
  1, i.e. sample normally — bypass it. Enable with `cache_max_entries` (+ optional
  `cache_ttl_seconds`, default 300s).
  A replay only carries headers that describe the stored payload (`content-type`,
  `X-Mainspring-Backend`/`-Device`/`-Warning`). The caller's own `X-Request-ID` and quota headroom come
  from this request, never from the leader's — no cross-tenant header ever replays.
- Path scope (what applies where): the admission pipeline — API-key auth, per-tenant rate + token budgets,
  the context guardrail, `clamp_max_tokens`, `precise_context`, the concurrency gate + queue, the circuit
  breaker, per-request timeouts, cost accounting, and now the response cache and request coalescing —
  applies to **both** the OpenAI endpoints and Anthropic `/v1/messages`. Each dialect caches its own wire
  shape (an Anthropic caller is replayed an Anthropic message), keyed by request path, so the two can
  never serve one another's bodies. Still OpenAI-path only: retry-with-backoff and model fallback chains.
- Cost accounting: optional per-model USD pricing (`input_usd_per_mtok` / `output_usd_per_mtok`, 0 =
  local/free) turns real token usage into spend. Cost lands in the usage ledger (`cost_usd`), a
  `mainspring_cost_usd_total{model}` /metrics counter, and per-model + total in /v1/quality — a real
  cost signal a trust control plane (Hydra) can route away from. Priced only from exact usage; never guessed.
- Observability: Prometheus `/metrics` (TTFT, prompt/output tokens, cost, requests, residency, inflight/queued,
  cache hits, resilience counters `mainspring_{retries,coalesced,fallback}_total`, and latency percentiles
  `mainspring_{duration,ttft,queue_wait}_ms_{p50,p90,p99}` — a bounded recent-sample reservoir estimate, not
  a mean) and an append-only JSONL usage ledger (each event records retries/coalesced/fallback too). Queue
  wait is the time a request actually spent queued for a concurrency-gate slot, measured separately from
  total duration so backpressure latency is distinguishable from real generation time. The same percentiles
  are in `/v1/quality` per model. Token counts are real when the upstream reports a usage object (non-stream
  body, or the streaming `include_usage` final chunk), else estimated — including an `/v1/embeddings`
  response, whose usage object carries `prompt_tokens` and no `completion_tokens`.
  Refusals are counted too, on **both** dialects: 503 backpressure, 503 circuit-open/backend-unavailable,
  429 token budget and 400 context-guardrail rejections all record an event with their real status — from
  the OpenAI endpoints and from Anthropic `/v1/messages`, which does its own budget/gate/breaker checks —
  and the ledger's `error_code` disambiguates causes that share one status. Cache hits and coalesced followers carry the latency the caller
  actually saw, not 0ms. In-flight and queue-depth counters are maintained whether or not the concurrency
  gate is enabled (it is off by default) — only the admission decision depends on `max_inflight`.
  The ledger reports whether it really opened: the startup banner warns loudly on a failed open instead of
  claiming an active ledger, `GET /admin/config` exposes `usage_ledger.active`, and the first write failure
  is logged rather than discarded.
- Config lint: catches config combinations that are valid YAML but silently do nothing — enforce_context/
  clamp_max_tokens/precise_context set but a model has no ctx (guardrail is a no-op for it), model_fallbacks
  targeting an unresolvable model/alias, a negative cost rate, or a missing tls_cert/tls_key file. Surfaced
  as `mainspring doctor` diagnostics, as non-fatal stderr warnings at `mainspring serve` startup, and live
  via `GET /admin/config`'s `lint_warnings` field — reflecting the config as of the last successful
  load/reload, not just startup, so an operator can check for silently-inert settings on a running server
  without digging through logs.
- Opt-in, verified managed install: never installs anything unless you run `mainspring install`, and
  every install is SHA-256-verified against an expected hash, refusing on a mismatch. Mainspring ships
  no curated artifact catalogue — the embedded manifest is empty by design, so you supply the artifact
  with `--url` + `--sha256`, or your own manifest file (optionally ed25519-signed via `--pubkey`).
  Running `mainspring install <backend>` with nothing supplied says so plainly rather than guessing.
- Deploy anywhere: single static binary, distroless container image, and a Helm chart (HPA,
  ServiceMonitor, GPU node scheduling). Optional TLS (tls_cert/tls_key => HTTPS, TLS 1.2 minimum).
- Graceful drain: `/readyz` flips to 503 on shutdown so load balancers stop routing while in-flight
  requests finish. It also flips to 503 (`degraded`) when the circuit breaker is enabled and every
  configured model's breaker is Open — a full-outage signal, not just an explicit drain — so a load
  balancer or Kubernetes readinessProbe stops sending traffic to a pod that cannot serve a single request.
  A single healthy or half-open (recovering) model keeps readyz at 200.
- Request correlation: every request carries an `X-Request-ID` (accepted from the client or generated,
  echoed on the response and recorded in the usage ledger); an optional JSONL access log records every
  request (tenant, method, path, status, duration) — the `tenant` field names the authenticated
  principal, so the log attributes an admin action to whoever performed it (omitted in open mode, where
  there is no principal, and for a rejected key). W3C `traceparent` is accepted/continued (or generated), the
  `trace_id` is recorded alongside `request_id`, and a child traceparent is forwarded to the engine so
  distributed traces stitch end to end — dependency-free, no OpenTelemetry SDK. The caller's trace flags
  are propagated unchanged, so a request that opted out of sampling is not sampled downstream; only a
  trace Mainspring mints itself is marked sampled.
- Hot reload: `SIGHUP` re-reads the config file and swaps models, aliases, and tenants without dropping
  in-flight requests or the listener; unsafe changes (listen address, backend set) require a restart and
  are logged. Unchanged models stay resident; changed/removed models are evicted and reload on demand —
  a model actively serving a request is never evicted mid-flight, even if its spec changed; eviction is
  deferred until it actually goes idle. Every other setting reload does not (or structurally cannot)
  re-apply — timeouts, cache, guardrail, clamp, retry, coalesce, breaker, per-model cost/fallback
  overrides, and more — is logged as requiring a restart when it changes, rather than silently keeping
  the old value with no explanation.
- Reload never weakens the running server: settings the config file cannot express are carried across
  it rather than dropped. Models given with `--model` and models found by auto-discovery survive a
  reload (the file wins on an id clash), and credentials given with `--api-key` are preserved. A reload
  whose config would leave the server with no tenants at all — i.e. would switch a running,
  authenticated server into open mode — is **refused** with an error and changes nothing, because the
  check runs before anything is applied. Open mode is only ever entered at startup, deliberately.

## Backends

- Managed (subprocess, opt-in install): `llamacpp` (llama-server), `mlx` (mlx_lm.server, Apple Silicon).
- Adopt-only (detect a running server; never installed): `ollama` (:11434), `lmstudio` (:1234),
  `llamafile` (:8080), `gpt4all` (:4891).

## CLI

- `mainspring serve` — start the server (flags: --addr, --config, --model id=path, --api-key,
  --backend, --max-loaded, --max-resident-mb, --max-inflight, --max-queue, --keep-alive, --usage-ledger,
  --tls-cert, --tls-key).
- `mainspring backends` — detect engines on this host (system vs managed).
- `mainspring models` — list configured models and their resolved backend.
- `mainspring install <backend>` — opt-in, checksum-verified engine install (--url/--sha256 or a
  signed manifest via --pubkey/--manifest-sig).
- `mainspring doctor` — diagnose backends, config, models, ports, accelerator.
- `mainspring version`.

## Endpoints

- `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/completions`, `POST /v1/embeddings`
- `POST /v1/messages` (Anthropic: text + tool use + images; streaming translated, incl. input_json_delta;
  `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k` and `stop_sequences` are all forwarded to the engine — `top_k` is not in
  the OpenAI schema but every engine Mainspring drives accepts it, so it is passed on rather than dropped)
- `GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/models/{id}` (OpenAI "retrieve a model"; resolves aliases; adds
  resident/backend/device/effective_ctx/degraded when the model is loaded), `GET /capabilities`,
  `GET /metrics`, `GET /healthz`, `GET /readyz`
- `GET /v1/quality` (optional Hydra routing signal: per-model resident/device/degraded/effective_ctx/
  inflight/queue_depth/ttft_ms_p50; admin-gated)
- Admin API (admin-gated; audited via the access log, whose `tenant` field names the admin who performed
  the action — in open mode there is no principal to record): `GET /admin/config` (effective runtime settings —
  timeouts, retry, breaker, cache, coalesce, guardrail, concurrency, fallbacks; secret-free by construction),
  `GET /admin/usage` (per-tenant consumption actuals — requests, prompt/output tokens, USD cost; open-mode
  traffic bucketed as "(anonymous)"), `POST /admin/drain[?on=false]`, `POST /admin/reload`,
  `POST /admin/models/{id}/load`, `POST /admin/models/{id}/unload` (force-stops the model regardless of
  in-flight requests — an explicit admin action always takes priority — and reports how many were actually
  interrupted via `interrupted_requests`, so the operator knows whether they just cut off live traffic),
  `POST /admin/breaker/{id}/reset`
  (force a tripped circuit breaker back to closed without waiting out the cooldown), `POST /admin/cache/clear`
  (purge the response cache on demand instead of waiting for TTL/LRU eviction; a no-op when caching is off)

## Errors

All errors are OpenAI-shaped `{"error":{"message","type","code"}}` with a stable machine-branchable
`code`: `invalid_request`, `context_length_exceeded`, `method_not_allowed`, `model_not_found`,
`unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `rate_limited`, `token_budget_exceeded`, `server_busy`, `circuit_open`,
`backend_unavailable`, `upstream_error`, `timeout`, `internal_error`. Same-status/different-cause
conditions are distinguished by `code` (503: server_busy vs circuit_open vs backend_unavailable;
400: invalid_request vs context_length_exceeded).

## Non-goals

- Mainspring does not build inference kernels — it wraps permissively-licensed engines.
- No GUI dependency; headless-first daemon.

## Relationship to Hydra

Two control planes at different scopes, not a router and a server. Hydra
(https://github.com/ankit373/hydra) is a provider-neutral *Trust* Control Plane: it routes across many
heads to a target confidence of correctness. Mainspring is the *inference* control plane for one head:
admission control, VRAM residency, and fail-loud truth about what actually ran. Hydra asks which head
should answer and how confident we are it is right; Mainspring answers what is true about this head
right now. They meet over the standard OpenAI-compatible boundary. Hydra works with everything
(Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and never depends on Mainspring —
Mainspring is simply the head it integrates with best. The optional `GET /v1/quality`
endpoint is that integration contract: a machine-readable per-model routing signal (residency, real
device, degraded state, effective context, in-flight/queue depth, TTFT p50) a trust control plane or router can consume to
route to Mainspring best. It is never required — Mainspring runs fine standalone with no router.
